# Go qualifier-type / type-facts arm allocation measurement record.
# darwin/arm64, Apple M4 Max, 16 procs, go1.26.4.
#
# ============================================================================
# READ THIS FIRST: THE GATE IS NO LONGER A RATIO. It is two ABSOLUTE per-leg
# allocation ceilings, and the ratchet_multiple key is RETIRED.
# ============================================================================
#
# WHY THE RATIO EXISTED, AND WHY IT STOPPED BEING JUSTIFIED. A ratio normalizes
# against a moving denominator, and this benchmark HAD one: it read
# chunker_identity.go, a live source file in the package under test, so an
# absolute number would have decayed on any ordinary edit to it. Measured,
# holding code constant and swapping only the input: 3823/5707 (1.4928) on the
# 447-line revision, 4022/5845 (1.4533) on a 481-line one. The input is now
# FROZEN at testdata/chunker_bench_input.go.txt, and that removes the ratio's
# entire justification. With a fixed input, an absolute count measures the thing
# actually at issue -- did the arm get more expensive -- and a ratio only adds
# failure modes.
#
# THE THREE FAILURE MODES A RATIO HAS AND AN ABSOLUTE CEILING DOES NOT:
#
#  1. IT IS RE-BASED BY ITS OWN INPUT. Shortening the fixture raises the ratio
#     for identical code, because arm_off shrinks faster than the arm's
#     per-declaration cost. The number moves with no code change.
#  2. IT IS DILUTED BY COST ADDED TO BOTH LEGS. A sibling lane's flow arm is
#     measured at 1182 allocations/op registered on BOTH legs. Folded into the
#     old 1.41 ratio it gave arm_off 5018 / arm_on 6562 = 1.3077, taking the
#     gate's slack from 28 to 513 allocations -- an 18.5x loss of sensitivity,
#     bought by adding cost. Under an absolute arm_on ceiling that same arm
#     lands as +1182 against a fixed number and is caught, not absorbed.
#  3. IT CAN PUNISH A GENUINE IMPROVEMENT. A shared helper made cheaper lowers
#     BOTH legs, and where the saving is symmetric that RAISES the ratio: at the
#     old margin, (5380-X)/(3836-X) crossed 1.41 at X = 71. That is what kept
#     findNodeByType, goSoleTypeSpec and extractGoInterfaceEmbeds on their
#     allocating string comparisons -- the instrument scored the improvement as
#     a regression.
#
# HONEST NOTE ON (3): WHEN THE CONVERSION WAS ACTUALLY TAKEN, THE RATIO WOULD
# HAVE IMPROVED, NOT DEGRADED. The X = 71 threshold models a helper whose saving
# lands EQUALLY on both legs. These three do not: they saved 13 on arm_off and
# 84 on arm_on, because the type-facts arm reaches goStructFieldTypes and
# goAllEmbeds in addition to the shared emitDeclarationEdges path. So the ratio
# would have moved 1.4021 -> 1.3853. The hazard in (3) is real for a
# symmetrically-shared helper and remains the right reason not to build a budget
# this way, but it did not fire here, and the earlier prediction that it would
# was wrong. Recorded rather than quietly dropped.
#
# THE TRAJECTORY, every row measured on the pinned fixture except the first:
#
#   tree                                     arm_off  arm_on   delta   note
#   ---------------------------------------  -------  ------  ------  -------------
#   integration branch before this work         3823    5707    1884  live input
#   same, measured on the pinned fixture        3836    5720    1884  +13 each leg
#   after the arm-exclusive reductions          3836    5379    1543  ratio era
#   after the shared-helper conversions         3824    5296    1473  this record
#
# arm_on falls 5720 -> 5296 (-424, -7.4%) and the arm's marginal cost 1884 ->
# 1473 (-21.8%). arm_off falls 3836 -> 3824 because the shared helpers are on
# its path too -- that is a real production saving on EVERY collect, and it is
# now credited rather than penalized.
#
# BEWARE ONE COINCIDENCE IN THAT TABLE. arm_off reads 3823 on the live input
# before any of this work and 3824 on the pinned fixture after all of it. Those
# are not the same measurement returning: the fixture ADDS 13 (one block comment
# chunk) and the shared-helper conversions REMOVE 13. Two independent moves that
# nearly cancel.
#
# THE FLOW ARM LANDED, AND IT CHANGED BOTH LEGS. A third Go arm (flow steps) is
# now registered in production, on BOTH the arm_off and arm_on legs, so both
# absolute numbers moved and the ceilings below are derived on the merged tree.
# An absolute ceiling SEES that cost, which is the whole reason for the shape:
# the retired ratio would have absorbed it.
#
# THE TWO ARMS ARE NOT ADDITIVE, and this is the measurement that settles a
# question two lanes could not answer by comparing numbers across trees. They
# SHARE the per-node cost of materializing Go wrappers for a declaration body,
# because Tree.cachedNode memoizes each node and whichever arm descends first
# pays for it. All four cells measured on ONE tree, allocs/op:
#
#                       flow OFF   flow ON
#     qual+tf OFF          3836      5945
#     qual+tf ON           5309      6241
#
#   qual+tf marginal, flow OFF : 1473
#   qual+tf marginal, flow ON  :  296   <- arm_on - arm_off, what the gate reads
#   flow    marginal, qual OFF : 2109
#   flow    marginal, qual ON  :  932   <- flow_on - flow_off
#
# The SHARED term is 1177 derived from either side independently, and
# 296 + 932 + 1177 = 2405 reconciles exactly to arm_on minus the both-off
# baseline. So registering the flow arm does not add a constant to both legs --
# it CUTS the qualifier+type-facts marginal cost from 1473 to 296.
#
# WHAT THAT MEANS FOR ANY arm_on-MINUS-arm_off FIGURE: it is not a property of
# the qualifier arm alone. It is that arm's marginal cost GIVEN WHAT ELSE IS
# REGISTERED, and it changes by 1177 depending on whether the flow arm is on.
# Two measurements of it taken on trees that differ in that respect are not
# comparable, and differencing them yields a number that looks like an
# unexplained cost source and is not one.
#
# DERIVATION OF THE TWO CEILINGS. Rule: the MAXIMUM allocs/op observed across a
# five-run batch on the final tree, rounded UP to the next multiple of ten, plus
# 20 allocations of headroom.
#
#   arm_on   max 6241 -> 6250 -> ceiling 6270   (slack 29)
#   arm_off  max 5945 -> 5950 -> ceiling 5970   (slack 25)
#
# Across that batch every leg read the SAME value on all five runs -- arm_off
# 5945, arm_on 6241, flow_off 5309, flow_on 6241 -- so the headroom is pure
# margin rather than jitter absorption, and still tight enough to fire on one
# extra allocation per declaration.
#
# THE TWO CEILINGS COVER ALL THREE ARMS between them, which is worth stating
# because only two legs are gated. arm_off runs with the flow arm ON, so a flow
# regression raises it; arm_on runs with EVERYTHING on, so it catches any of the
# three. There is no arm whose cost lands outside both numbers.
#
# arm_off IS A CONTROL LEG, NOT DECORATION. Its constancy at 3836/3837 through
# every arm-exclusive reduction is what proved those reductions did not touch
# the shared path. Gating it makes that an assertion rather than an observation:
# if arm_off moves, either the fixture changed or a shared path did, and the
# arm_on number is no longer comparable to the one recorded here. A moved
# arm_off should be read as "re-derive both", never as "raise arm_off".
#
# THE ns/op LEG IS DROPPED, and this costs real coverage, so the reasoning is
# recorded rather than assumed. It was a 1.25x ratio of the two legs' wall time,
# and it failed on both counts. It was NEARLY BLIND to what it guarded:
# tree-sitter parsing dominates ChunkFile's wall time, so when this arm's
# allocations rose 79% the ns/op reading moved +4.1% -- the measured fact that
# caused the allocation gate to be added in the first place. And it FLAPPED: on
# a machine running parallel lanes it read 0.940, 0.961, 1.016, 1.077 and 1.168
# across runs whose allocation counts were bit-identical, and one starved run
# read 1.69 and failed the gate outright. A gate that cannot see the regression
# it guards, and that reds on machine load, trains people to ignore reds. WHAT
# IS LOST: this benchmark now carries NO wall-time guard at all, so a change
# that is slow without allocating -- a hot loop over already-materialized nodes,
# a quadratic scan -- would not be caught here. Allocation count is a good proxy
# for this particular arm, whose work is allocation-bound, and a poor one in
# general.
#
# ARM OUTPUT IDENTITY is asserted separately and is the property that makes an
# arm_on/arm_off ratio meaningful at all: TestGoArmsEmitIdenticalChunksAndEdges
# pins that both legs emit the SAME 143 chunks and 232 edges on this fixture,
# with the armed leg carrying 12 composed signatures and the unarmed leg none.
# Without it a "reduction" could be a behavior change wearing a performance
# change's clothes, and a ratio could compare two different outputs.
#
# AND THE REDUCTIONS THEMSELVES WERE CHECKED AGAINST A REAL CORPUS, which is the
# stronger oracle because it compares the arm's output BEFORE and AFTER rather
# than one leg against the other. TestGoQualifierOutputDigest was run with
# QUALID_ROOT pointed at one fixed unmodified checkout, once from the tree at
# 44f42093 and once from this tree, so both runs chunked byte-identical input:
#
#   pre-change  98663 lines  a3cf4f7ddd66df1f54cccef84ea3ac15727b8eac995fffdeb4267d2c5da4863b
#   post-change 98663 lines  a3cf4f7ddd66df1f54cccef84ea3ac15727b8eac995fffdeb4267d2c5da4863b
#
# Identical, to the byte, across every QualifierTypes binding and every
# TypeFacts record the two arms produce for that corpus. Pointing QUALID_ROOT at
# a THIRD tree is what makes the comparison valid: run against this working tree
# the digest would differ for the trivial reason that this changeset edits files
# that are themselves part of the corpus.
#
# THAT ORACLE WAS NOT SUFFICIENT FOR THE SHARED-HELPER CONVERSIONS, and the gap
# is worth naming: it digests QT and TF lines only. findNodeByKind,
# findTypeIdentifier, qualifiedTypeName and extractGoEmbeds decide EMBEDS edges
# and, through extractGoReceiver, the receiver-qualified node ID of every Go
# method -- none of which appear in those lines. A second before/after digest
# was therefore taken over the same fixed corpus, covering every CHUNK (type,
# parent, name, line range, signature), every declaration's Embeds/IsInterface/
# IsGeneric, and every EDGE (type, endpoints, weight):
#
#   pre-conversion   3568 files  439483 lines  5bf7dcdfd1b5104bbc90cbdbf7560d049eef8850bb1e17f27f657a1a8c38511f
#   post-conversion  3568 files  439483 lines  5bf7dcdfd1b5104bbc90cbdbf7560d049eef8850bb1e17f27f657a1a8c38511f
#
# Identical. The instrument was a throwaway test present in both trees and
# removed afterwards, which is why it is recorded here rather than checked in:
# it answers one question about one refactor, and a permanent digest of every
# chunk in a corpus would red on every legitimate chunker change.
#
# ============================================================================
# PRIOR DERIVATION, kept for provenance. Every number in the block below was
# measured against the LIVE chunker_identity.go and is superseded by the pinned
# figures above. The candidate comparison is still the record of WHY the
# Symbol()-not-Type() mechanism is the one worth applying, which is why it is
# retained rather than deleted.
# ============================================================================
#
# FOUR-CANDIDATE COMPARISON. allocs/op and ns/op on both instruments.
#
#   candidate      arm_on      arm_on ns     walk        walk ns    identity
#                  allocs/op   (mean)        allocs/op   (mean)     (both corpora)
#   -------------  ----------  ------------  ----------  ---------  -------------
#   baseline       7201        8506231       2041        277853     (is the baseline)
#   C1 alone       5447        8468091       287         253214     MATCH
#   C2 alone       5447        8695892       287         285893     ties C1 exactly
#   C3 alone       7201        8371734       2041        273804     MATCH
#   C4 on C1       5445        8666462       285         255349     MATCH
#   C1+C4 (kept)   5445        8666462       285         255349     MATCH
#
# READ THE ns/op COLUMN WITH CARE AND DO NOT RANK CANDIDATES BY IT. Each figure
# is the mean of that candidate's own run batch (n=1 for the baseline, n=2 for
# C2 and C3, n=3 for C1 and C4), and the batches were taken minutes apart on a
# machine doing other work: the SAME kept tree measured 8425512 in one batch and
# 8666462 in another, a 2.9% spread that is larger than most of the differences
# between rows. The ALLOCATION columns are the trustworthy ones - they were
# IDENTICAL on every repeat of every candidate, to the allocation - which is
# exactly why the budget this ticket ratchets is a ratio of allocations and not
# of time, and why the ns/op ceiling is left at its untouched 1.25x.
#
# SELECTION, applied mechanically to the numbers above.
#   C1 KEPT  - 5447 < 7201, digests match. The whole reduction is the per-node
#              cgo C-string conversion the walk paid for Node.Type().
#   C2 NEVER KEPT by the rule, and the measurement says why rather than the
#              reasoning: it ties C1 exactly on both instruments (5447 / 287)
#              because Type() allocates INSIDE the binding
#              (bindings.go:455, C.GoString(C.ts_node_type)), so there is
#              nothing left to intern; the only key obtainable is Symbol()
#              (bindings.go:450, a scalar), and holding Symbol() the string is
#              not needed at all. It is C1 plus a map hash. It is rejected on
#              the rule (a redundant second spelling of one mechanism), not on
#              the ns/op column, which is too noisy between batches to rank on.
#   C3 NOT KEPT - 7201, which is the baseline exactly. Zero allocation
#              reduction. A visit census over 3,364 Go files measured why: of
#              2,406,853 named-node visits under full recursion, a conservative
#              denylist of kinds that provably cannot contain a func_literal,
#              var_declaration, const_declaration or short_var_declaration
#              skips 5,095 nodes - 0.21%. The denylisted kinds are already
#              leaves. Identity was MATCH on both corpora, so C3 is safe; it is
#              simply worth nothing.
#   C4 KEPT  - 5445 < 7201, digests match. Two allocations, from the 2 of 13
#              declarations in the benchmark input that bind nothing.
#
# WINNER = c1+c4. Ratio 5445/4013 = 1.3568, which is what the superseded 1.41
# was derived from.
